title: Novel Dietary Interventions in Functional Dyspepsia
official: Novel Dietary Interventions in Functional Dyspepsia
summary:
This pilot study will test whether people with functional dyspepsia can follow two new dietary approaches and whether these diets may improve symptoms. Thirty adults will be randomly assigned to follow a low-histidine diet, a low-tryptophan diet, or a comparison diet for six weeks. The study aims to reduce-not eliminate- intake. The comparison diet provides dietary instructions that are not intended to reduce either nutrient.

The main goal is to determine whether participants intake of these nutrients can change through diet approaches.

Participants will receive nutrition counseling, follow the diet assigned, describe food consumption during dietary-recall interviews, complete questionnaires, provide blood and urine samples, and swallow a capsule that measures movement and gases in the digestive tract before and after the intervention.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* meeting Rome IV criteria for Functional dyspepsia (FD)
* planned esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) as part of clinical care

Exclusion Criteria:

* Documented drug or alcohol use disorder
* Documented history of an eating disorder
* Habitual vegetarian or vegan diet
* Currently pregnant or breastfeeding or anticipating pregnancy during study period
* Unwilling to follow a low histidine or low tryptophan diet
* Unexplained weight loss, dysphagia, or other warning signs that would prompt evaluation with esophagogastroduodenoscopy - if present would need to ensure no evidence of Los Angeles (LA) grade C or D esophagitis or peptic ulcer disease on EGD performed as part of clinical care
* Use of daily opioid pain medication or glucagon-like peptide receptor 1(GLP-1) agonist
* Current use of metoclopramide or other prokinetic medication
* History of gastrointestinal surgery
* Poorly controlled diabetes mellitus (HgbA1c \>10%)
* Known allergy to ingredient in Atmo Motility Bar (Rolled oats, glucose syrup, soy nuggets, rice bran crisps, brown rice syrup, pea protein powder, glycerine, natural vanilla extract and monkfruit juice extract)
* Inability to swallow pills the size of large vitamins
